gaps.sentence: 'Thank you for delivering it so quickly,' she said. She ___ me for delivering it so quickly.
gaps.explanation: Thanks are reported as thank somebody for + -ing.

gaps.sentence: 'I'm about to leave,' he said at six. At six he said he ___ about to leave.
gaps.explanation: 'Be about to' backshifts like any present form: am about to → was about to.

gaps.sentence: 'I'm sorry I shouted at you,' he said. He ___ shouting at me.
gaps.explanation: Apologies take apologise for + -ing: apologised for shouting.

gaps.sentence: "Can you help me?" — She asked ___ help her.
'Don't be late again,' the coach told him. The coach told him ___ late again.
gaps.explanation: Negative commands: not to be, with the negative before the whole infinitive.

gaps.sentence: 'I'll be waiting outside the cinema,' he said. He said he ___ waiting outside the cinema.
gaps.explanation: will be + -ing becomes would be + -ing in reported speech.

gaps.sentence: "I saw him yesterday." — He said he ___ him the day before.
gaps.explanation: Backshift one step: saw → had seen; yesterday → the day before.

gaps.sentence: 'I'm meeting them tomorrow evening,' she said. She said she was meeting them ___ evening.
gaps.explanation: Tomorrow evening becomes the next (or the following) evening.
